2027-01-31.title: Fifth Sunday of Denha
2027-01-31.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: I am the LORD your God, who teaches you and leads you
The light has come into the world
2027-01-31.alt: Season of Denha. St John Bosco: Philippians 4:4–9; Matthew 18:1–5.
2027-01-31.verse: “For God so loved the world that he gave his only Son, so that everyone who believes in him may not perish but may have eternal life.
theo: As Israel stands at the edge of the promised land, Moses warns them not to seek the future through soothsayers and diviners, as the nations do: “You must remain completely loyal to the LORD your God.” Instead God makes a promise: “The LORD your God will raise up for you a prophet like me from among your own people; you shall heed such a prophet.” At Horeb the people had been terrified by the fire and the voice, and God answered their fear with tenderness: “I will put my words in the mouth of the prophet, who shall speak to them everything that I command.” Israel waited for that prophet for centuries. In Isaiah the same God speaks to his exiles in Babylon: “I am the LORD your God, who teaches you for your own good, who leads you in the way you should go. O that you had paid attention to my commandments! Then your prosperity would have been like a river.” God is not a distant force to be manipulated by horoscopes and lucky times; he is a teacher who wants to lead us.

In the Gospel the Prophet like Moses speaks at night to Nicodemus. He recalls a strange scene from the wilderness: when the people were dying from serpent bites, Moses lifted up a bronze serpent on a pole, and whoever looked at it lived. “And just as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, so must the Son of Man be lifted up, that whoever believes in him may have eternal life.” The Cross is the pole, and the One lifted up is the Son. Then comes the verse that sums up the whole Gospel: “For God so loved the world that he gave his only Son, so that everyone who believes in him may not perish but may have eternal life.” God did not send his Son “to condemn the world, but in order that the world might be saved through him.” Judgment is not God's revenge; it is our choice: “the light has come into the world, and people loved darkness rather than light.”

Hebrews encourages Christians who have grown tired: “God is not unjust; he will not overlook your work and the love that you showed for his sake in serving the saints.” Do not become sluggish; imitate “those who through faith and patience inherit the promises.” Abraham waited long, and “having patiently endured, obtained the promise.” Denha reveals Christ as the Prophet who speaks God's words, the Son lifted up for our healing, and the Light that shows our deeds as they are. “But those who do what is true come to the light.” Today the Church also remembers St John Bosco, who brought countless poor boys of Turin out of the streets and into the light of Christ, with patience, joy and a deep love for the Eucharist and Our Lady.
conn: The people asked John the Baptist, “Are you the prophet?” (John 1:21); Peter applied Deuteronomy 18 to Jesus (Acts 3:22).
Deuteronomy 18 forbids seeking the future through divination; the Church likewise rejects horoscopes, astrology and recourse to mediums (CCC 2115–2116).
Numbers 21:8–9. Wisdom 16:6–7 calls it a symbol of deliverance: it was not the image that saved but God, the Saviour of all.
In John the word means both crucifixion and exaltation (John 8:28; 12:32): the Cross is Christ's throne of glory.
He came to Jesus in the dark (John 3:2) and later came to the light, bringing myrrh and aloes for Jesus' burial (John 19:39).
The oath to Abraham (Genesis 22:16–17) shows that God's promise cannot fail; Hebrews calls our hope an anchor of the soul (Hebrews 6:19).
altar: The Son lifted up on the Cross is lifted up again in the hands of the priest before Communion, so that all who look on him with faith may have life.
At every Holy Qurbana the Prophet like Moses speaks God's word to us, and the Light of the world gives himself as food.

live: Remove any horoscope, lucky charm or reliance on auspicious times from your life, and trust God's providence.
Spend five minutes each day this week looking at a crucifix in silence.
Bring one hidden fault to the sacrament of Reconciliation.
Spend time with a young person, encouraging them in faith or study.
fathers: Those bitten in the wilderness looked at the serpent and lived; so those wounded by sin look in faith on the death of Christ and are healed.
He did not give a servant, nor an angel, but his only Son: the greatness of the gift shows the greatness of the love.
magis: The Word became flesh so that we might know God's love: God so loved the world.
Christ came not to condemn but to save; whoever rejects the grace offered judges himself.
Divination, horoscopes and astrology contradict the honour and trust we owe to God alone.
Hope, the anchor of the soul, sustained by God's promise.
Christ, the Word made flesh, perfects and completes revelation.
saints: 2 Feb: Presentation of the Lord. 3 Feb: St Blaise. Fifth week of Denha continues.
2027-01-31.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, Prophet like Moses and only Son of the Father, you were lifted up on the Cross so that all who believe in you may have eternal life. Free us from every superstition and every darkness, teach us and lead us in the way we should go, give us patience to inherit your promises, and through the prayers of St John Bosco help us bring the young into your light. Glory to you, with the Father and the Holy Spirit, for ever. Amen.

quick: God gives a prophet like Moses; we do not need diviners.
God so loved the world that he gave his only Son, lifted up for our healing.
The light has come; those who do what is true come to the light.
2027-01-31.action: Spend five minutes in silence before a crucifix today.
2027-01-31.question: Is there any darkness I am keeping away from the light?
catechism: Christ came to save, not to condemn.
kidsaint: He was a priest in Turin who loved poor boys who had no home. He gave them school, games, work and Jesus. Lesson: we can help other children come close to Jesus!
2027-01-31.special: Fifth Sunday of Denha. St John Bosco.
term: John's word for Jesus being raised on the Cross and, through the Cross, raised in glory.

family.explain: Long ago, when people were bitten by snakes, God told Moses to lift up a bronze snake on a pole, and whoever looked at it got well. Jesus was lifted up on the Cross so that everyone who looks to him with faith can live for ever. God loves the world that much!
family.intention: We pray for children and young people, through St John Bosco.
family.ask: Ask: “Can we put a crucifix where our family will see it every day?”

illus: A family in Changanassery used to fix every journey and function by the almanac's auspicious hours. When their son's wedding date was set, the grandfather said: this time, let us ask only for God's blessing. They prayed together before the crucifix and kept the date the parish could give. The son later said it was the first time he understood that God is not a lucky charm but a Father who leads us.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, lifted up for our salvation, draw us into your light as we gather. Amen.
share: The LORD your God will raise up for you a prophet like me (Deuteronomy 18:15). Do I listen to Jesus, or to other voices about my future?
So must the Son of Man be lifted up (John 3:14). Do I look at the Cross with faith?
Those who do what is true come to the light (John 3:21). What do I need to bring into the light?
pm.resp: Lord, lead us into your light.
interc: For the Church, that she may proclaim God's love for the world.
For those trapped in superstition and fear.
For those who live in darkness and sin.
For young people, through St John Bosco.
For our group, that we may come to the light.
pm.close: Father, you so loved the world that you gave your only Son. Draw us to him lifted up, and lead us in the way we should go. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, Moses tells Israel not to seek the future from soothsayers and diviners, but to trust God's promise: the LORD your God will raise up for you a prophet like me from among your own people; you shall heed such a prophet (Deuteronomy 18:15).

Through Isaiah, God says: I am the LORD your God, who teaches you for your own good, who leads you in the way you should go (Isaiah 48:17). God is not a power to be managed by horoscopes and lucky times. He is a Father who teaches and leads.

In the Gospel Jesus, the Prophet like Moses, tells Nicodemus: just as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, so must the Son of Man be lifted up, that whoever believes in him may have eternal life (John 3:14–15).

And then the heart of the Gospel: God so loved the world that he gave his only Son (John 3:16). He did not come to condemn but to save. Judgment happens when we prefer darkness; salvation, when we come to the light.
Hebrews tells us not to become sluggish, but to imitate those who through faith and patience inherit the promises (Hebrews 6:12), like Abraham, who waited and obtained the promise.
Let us look at the Cross, leave every superstition, and bring our deeds into the light. And like St John Bosco, let us bring the young to Christ. Amen.
kids: Children, God loves the whole world so much that he gave us Jesus! Jesus was lifted up on the Cross so that we can live with him for ever.
Look at a cross today and say: thank you, Jesus!

intro: Theme: “For God so loved the world that he gave his only Son.”
Christ revealed as the Prophet like Moses, the Son lifted up, and the Light of the world.

q: The LORD your God will raise up for you a prophet like me from among your own people; you shall heed such a prophet.
While he was still speaking, suddenly a bright cloud overshadowed them, and from the cloud a voice said, “This is my Son, the Beloved; with him I am well pleased; listen to him!”
points.apply: Put away every horoscope and lucky charm; listen to Christ.

points.h: The God who teaches and leads
q: Thus says the LORD, your Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel: I am the LORD your God, who teaches you for your own good, who leads you in the way you should go.
Jesus said to him, “I am the way, and the truth, and the life. No one comes to the Father except through me.
points.apply: Ask God each morning this week to lead you in the way you should go.

q: So Moses made a serpent of bronze, and put it upon a pole; and whenever a serpent bit someone, that person would look at the serpent of bronze and live.
And just as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, so must the Son of Man be lifted up, that whoever believes in him may have eternal life.
points.apply: Spend five minutes daily before a crucifix.

q: The LORD is my light and my salvation; whom shall I fear? The LORD is the stronghold of my life; of whom shall I be afraid?
But those who do what is true come to the light, so that it may be clearly seen that their deeds have been done in God.”

concl: God has spoken in his Son and lifted him up for our salvation.
Leave the darkness, look at the Cross, and come to the light.
2027-01-31.resolve: Go to confession this week and place a crucifix where your family will see it.
